label: SIMULATION - not a measurement
what: What the MLX90640 thermal camera (55 x 35 degrees, 32 x 24 pixels) would show of a 1 m heat source on flat ground, seen from straight above.

sensor.accuracy: about 1 C (Pimoroni); the Melexis datasheet adds: only when the object fills the pixel's view, under settled conditions, and +-2 % of the difference from the sensor's own temperature
sensor.noise_source: Melexis MLX90640 datasheet rev 11 Table 14: 1 Hz RMS noise averages 0.14 K and 0.25 K (larger used); x sqrt(2) for the payload's 2 Hz is my assumption

detector.code: Shad-Drone-Payload/hotspots.py find_hotspots (4-connected pixels), defaults from payload.py

maths: footprint = 2 x height x tan(FOV/2) (Shad-Drone-Payload/geo.py, same as the guide's coverage calculator); each pixel mixes target and ground by the share of its footprint the target covers, mixed in 8-14 um infrared brightness
placement: Main grids: the target centred where four pixels meet (a fair case). Also reported: centred on one pixel (hotter peak, but fewer pixels, so it can miss the 3-pixel rule).

targets.name: Burning campfire
targets.source: Fraser, Choo, Kimble, Sutch, 'The morning after the night before: campfires revisited', Med J Aust 2003; 178(1): 30 (https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2003/178/1/morning-after-night-campfires-revisited): 'Each of the fires burned at greater than 510oC.' 510 C is the lowest value they give; the 1 m size is my choice ('campfire-sized').

targets.name: Campfire buried in sand, 8 hours later
targets.source: Same study: 'After 8 hours, the mean temperature was 91°C (range, 77°–118°C).' Read through a small hole in the sand, so it is a stand-in: the sand's own surface is probably cooler (not measured).

not_simulated: smoke and steam between the fire and the camera
emissivity (every surface treated as a perfect emitter)
sun-heated rocks, roofs, roads or vehicles
lens blur (the real pixel edges are soft, which spreads and lowers a small hot spot further)
drone tilt, height error and motion during the 0.5 s frame
trees, grass or anything covering the fire
real fires: a campfire is not a flat 1 m disc at one temperature
